title: De Mysteriis (Greek-English, Dillon and Clarke 2003)
author: Iamblichus
description: De Mysteriis (On the Mysteries) by Iamblichus of Chalcis (c. 245-325 CE), in the Greek-English edition with translation, introduction and notes by Emma C. Clarke, John M. Dillon and Jackson P. Hershbell (Society of Biblical Literature, Writings from the Greco-Roman World, 2003). Written under the persona of the Egyptian priest Abamon, it replies to Porphyry's sceptical Letter to Anebo questioning the reality and efficacy of ritual. Iamblichus defends theurgy, the 'divine work' of sacrifice, prayer, divination and sacred symbols, arguing that the soul cannot reach union with the gods by philosophy alone but through rites the gods themselves have given. He sets out a hierarchy of gods, daemons, heroes and souls, and discusses divination, Egyptian and Chaldean theology, and the nature of the divine. The most important document of theurgic Neoplatonism, it shaped Proclus, the Renaissance revival of magic and modern esoteric ritual theory.
